confirmed.statement: S1 counts people: 276 U.S.-based Prolific participants 'who contributed a total of 428 idea refinements'. The 276 are people and the 428 are outputs; the form keeps 276 as participants.n_analyzed and 428 as n_units of S1-O1.

All 276 are in the analysis. Table 2 prints N = 428 for all six models, and endnote 5 says N is 'the total number of idea refinements submitted across all ideators'. Because 428 equals the 276 participants' total, no participant's refinements were dropped, so 276 is the analyzed count.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 10 (article p. 9), Table 2 notes; PDF p. 14 (article p. 13), endnote 5; PDF p. 9 (article p. 8), Section 4.2

confirmed.statement: Each participant contributes at least one analyzed row: the Figure 3 note says 'Each participant provided one idea', and endnote 4 says the authors 'scored the first refinement of all ideas'.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 9 (article p. 8), Figure 3 note; PDF p. 14 (article p. 13), endnote 4

confirmed.statement: No participant was lost to missing survey controls: Models 1b and 1c add survey-measured controls (trait creativity, perceived mental outcome simulation, perceived ease of use, age), and N stays 428.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 10 (article p. 9), Section 4.3.5 and Table 2

confirmed.statement: People were the unit of assignment and all three cells are analyzed: a 'three-cell, between-subjects online experiment'; 'we randomly assigned ideators to experimental groups'; the backward-difference contrasts in Table 2 cover textual vs visual and visual vs control.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 8 (article p. 7), Section 4.1; PDF p. 13 (article p. 12), Section 6.3; PDF p. 9 (article p. 8), Section 4.3.1; PDF p. 10 (article p. 9), Table 2

confirmed.statement: The form's nulls and 'None reported' are correct: the 16 pages give no count at assignment, no arm sizes, and no exclusions, attention checks, dropouts, or attrition. Figures 4 and 5 show marginal means with 95% CIs and no Ns. The only cross-arm statement is that demographics showed no systematic differences across conditions.
confirmed.locator: All 16 PDF pages read, plus a search of the PDF text layer and the markdown; PDF p. 11 (article p. 10), Figures 4 and 5; PDF p. 9 (article p. 8), Section 4.2

confirmed.statement: The S1 'who' field matches the source: mean age 41.3, 43.8% female, 77.8% with at least a bachelor's degree, 74.2% working full or part time; US$2 pay and a US$4 bonus for the 10 best ideas.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 9 (article p. 8), Section 4.2; PDF p. 8 (article p. 7), Section 4.1

confirmed.statement: S2 is 'a separate Prolific sample' that used ChatGPT freely. The main text gives no size, country, demographics, or exclusions, so the form's null counts and not_stated country are right. S2's comparison arm is ideas from the S1 textual and visual arms, so the same S1 people appear in both studies and S2 adds no people to S1, as the form says.
The 88 Prolific workers who rated 158 ideas validate the creativity score. They are raters, not experimental participants, and the form does not count them.

No other paper is named as using these participants. The reference list does not cite the team's ICIS 2023 short paper (candidate c778; Gordetzki, Blohm, Hofstetter), whose public abstract describes a different manipulation (numeric and visual feedback and its timing) and states no sample. Overlap with c778 cannot be checked from either text.
Criterion 2 holds on S1 alone: 276 people analyzed across the three randomized arms, well above 50.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 9 (article p. 8), Section 4.2; PDF p. 10 (article p. 9), Table 2

summary: The form's people counts hold: S1 analyzed 276 Prolific participants (people, not the 428 refinements), Table 2's N = 428 equals their total refinements 'submitted across all ideators', and the paper gives no count at assignment, no arm sizes, no exclusions, and no S2 size, as the form's nulls record. S1 alone has well over 50 people analyzed, so criterion 2 holds, and the one open point, a possible overlap with the same team's ICIS 2023 short paper (c778), cannot be settled from either text and does not affect eligibility.
